barrel of a gun|guster.note: Featured on the 1999 album Lost and Gone Forever, where all the drums were played by hand without sticks, this track captures the listener's memory of seeing the Boston band open for Barenaked Ladies in the mid-'90s with their signature hand percussion and '4, 3, 2, 1' hook. basket case|green day.note: "Basket Case" is a song by the American rock band Green Day, released on August 1, 1994, by Reprise Records as the second single from the band's third studio album, Dookie. brick|ben folds five.note: Released by alternative rock group Ben Folds Five as a single from their album Whatever and Ever Amen, Brick became one of the band's biggest hits with mainstream radio play in the US, the UK, and Australia. colors|halsey.note: Released as a single from her debut studio album Badlands, Colors showcases the modern synth-pop style that initially drew this listener to Halsey's music. crazy for you|madonna.note: Written by John Bettis and Jon Lind and produced by John Jellybean Benitez, this pop ballad with torch song influences marked a departure from Madonna's earlier dance-oriented material and reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100. deep cover|dr. dre and snoop dogg.note: Serving as the debut solo single by American rapper and producer Dr. Dre and his first track released after the breakup of N.W.A, the song also features fellow American rapper Snoop Doggy Dogg in his first appearance on a record release. desperately wanting|better than ezra.note: Desperately Wanting is a song by American alternative rock group Better Than Ezra that was released in November 1996 as the second single from their third studio album, Friction, Baby, and became a chart hit in the United States, Australia, and Canada. enjoy the silence|depeche mode.note: Released as the second single from the album Violator, this track became Depeche Mode's best-selling single and won Best British Single at the Brit Awards 1991. eye of the tiger|survivor.note: Written by Frankie Sullivan and Jim Peterik as the theme song for the 1982 film Rocky III and released that May as a single from Survivor's third album, Eye of the Tiger, the track combines hard rock with a post-disco beat and reached number one on the charts of many countries. This listener associates the arena rock track with early musical memories tied to movies, specifically recalling boxing scenes and a later film featuring Ivan Drago.

footloose|kenny loggins.note: Co-written and recorded by American singer-songwriter Kenny Loggins, the track became a major chart-topper and received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song. heartspark dollarsign|everclear.note: Originally appearing on Everclear's 1995 major-label debut album Sparkle and Fade, "Heartspark Dollarsign" serves as a nostalgic anchor for the listener, recalling a bittersweet Boston Xmas rave concert that marked one of the final shows shared with a college roommate.

here comes a regular|the replacements.note: Here Comes a Regular appears on the 1985 album Tim, which was produced by Tommy Erdelyi and marked the final album featuring the original line-up of the band. hey ya|outkast.note: Performed by André 3000, "Hey Ya!" received critical acclaim and is consistently ranked as one of the greatest songs of the 2000s, reaching number one in multiple countries including the United States, Australia, and Canada. i think we're alone now|tiffany.note: Tiffany released her cover of I Think We're Alone Now as the second single from her debut studio album, Tiffany, and the track spent two weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. love song|the cure.note: Released in 1989 as part of The Cure's landmark album Disintegration, "Lovesong" became the band's highest-charting single on the US Billboard Hot 100. mayonaise|smashing pumpkins.note: Released in 1993 on the Smashing Pumpkins' breakthrough album Siamese Dream, "Mayonaise" remains one of the band's most celebrated alternative rock anthems. more than words|extreme.note: Released as an acoustic rock ballad by the American rock band Extreme from their second album, Pornograffitti, this song topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart. my name is jonas|weezer.note: Serving as the explosive opening track to Weezer's 1994 self-titled debut, 'My Name Is Jonas' transitions seamlessly from gentle acoustic picking into a heavy, melodic rock anthem. nightswimming|r.e.m..note: Originally released as a single in July 1993, the track features singer Michael Stipe accompanied by Mike Mills on piano, string arrangements by John Paul Jones, and oboe by Deborah Workman. papercut|linkin park.note: Released as the third single from Linkin Park's diamond-certified 2000 debut album Hybrid Theory, "Papercut" peaked at number 14 on the UK Singles Chart. so what'cha want|beastie boys.note: So What'Cha Want is a song by American hip-hop and rap rock group the Beastie Boys that also appears in the video game Rock Band 2. summer|buffalo tom.note: Buffalo Tom pursued a stripped-down, live-sounding approach for the album featuring this track, moving away from a polished sound. teenage love|slick rick.note: Teenage Love is the first single released from Slick Rick's 1988 debut album and was produced by Slick Rick and The Bomb Squad. The listener associates this track with an awkward adolescent period of yearning for a girlfriend and trying to find oneself.
